summary.title: A Practical Introduction to Blockchain with Python
summary.one_liner: Learn how blockchains work (double-spending, hashing, proof of work, conflict resolution) and see a basic RSA-signed blockchain with wallets and nodes implemented in Python and Flask.
keywords: bitcoin wallet private key public key
takeaways: Bitcoin's blockchain solves double-spending with a distributed, append-only, cryptographically signed ledger secured by proof of work.
Blocks are chained by including the previous block's SHA-256 hash, so changing old data invalidates later blocks.
Mining means finding a nonce whose hash meets a difficulty condition; the longest chain wins when nodes conflict.
The tutorial implements a Python/Flask blockchain with RSA-signed transactions, wallet generation, multiple nodes and conflict resolution.
The code is for education only and is not production-grade, per the author.
summary.summary: The article is a practical introduction to blockchain, using Bitcoin as the example. It first explains the double-spending problem, how Bitcoin's distributed ledger addresses it, and the steps of sending bitcoin. It then covers public-key cryptography, SHA-256 hashing, proof-of-work mining, chaining blocks, conflict resolution, and double-spending attacks, with interactive mining simulators. The final section walks through a Python implementation with Flask: an RSA wallet and transaction client plus a blockchain node with proof of work, signature checks, and node synchronization. The author notes the code is for educational use only and not for production.
